digest_markdown:
• 56 distinct supply chain attacks were tracked and alerted on by the StepSecurity threat intelligence team over the last 12 months, with every incident being a real compromise. [1]
• Software supply chain attacks target components that organizations and developers already trusted, compromising next versions of trusted packages or existing versions where the ecosystem allows tags to be silently repointed. [2]
• A supply chain attack can infect as many victims as possible, while hardware supply chain attacks compromise physical components for the same purpose. [2]
• The average software project has 203 dependencies, and a single compromised dependency can compromise every business that downloads from the vendor, resulting in exponential growth of victims. [2]
• A poisoned LiteLLM version on PyPI exposed 2,488 companies and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines on March 24, 2026. [4]
